_note: The DSX Scene LIGHTING corpus (dsx-scene.md P5): point lights + fog as pinned math. THE POINT FALLOFF LAW: attenuation(d, range) = window²/(1 + d²) with window = max(0, 1 − (d/range)⁴) — 1 at d = 0, exactly 0 at and past range (inverse-square with a smooth range window). THE LIT-COLOR LAW (the shared flat-Lambert model, P5-extended): lit = base · (ambient + dirColor·max(0, n·dirL) + Σ colorᵢ·intensityᵢ·att(dᵢ)·max(0, n·Lᵢ)), channels clamped to [0,1]. THE CAP: at most 4 point lights (SCENE_MAX_POINT_LIGHTS), first in document order; extras drop with one diagnostic. Root-level lights only — a light nested in a group is the NAMED ABSENCE of this phase. THE LINEAR FOG LAW (fog="#color near far" on <scene>, far > near or the whole attribute rejects with one diagnostic): f = clamp((far − d)/(far − near), 0, 1) for d = eye→fragment distance; final = f·lit + (1 − f)·fogColor. Floats 6 decimals, tolerance 1.5e-6; numbers from an independent scratch implementation. Runners: TS (per-PR). Kotlin/Swift are the NAMED P5 follow-up.

cases.name: attenuation — 1 at zero, windowed inverse-square, 0 at and past range
one point light — lit = base·(ambient + color·intensity·att·n·L)
two point lights sum; the grazing light contributes by its cosine
directional + point compose in one lit fold
the cap — five authored point lights parse to four + one diagnostic
fog factor — 1 before near, linear between, 0 past far
